name: Groundnut Rust
description: A fungal rust disease that produces orange-brown pustules on groundnut leaves. It is wind-borne and can spread rapidly, especially when leaf spot is also present, causing severe defoliation.
symptoms: Small orange to reddish-brown pustules primarily on lower leaf surfaces
Pustules rupturing to release powdery rust spores
Severe infection can kill plants prematurely
Stem and petiole lesions in heavy infections
causes: Extended leaf wetness from dew or rain
Survival on volunteer groundnut plants between seasons
treatments: Apply fungicides containing tebuconazole or propiconazole at first signs
Use sulfur-based fungicides as preventive treatment
Apply triadimefon for early rust control
prevention: Practice crop rotation with non-host crops
Ensure adequate plant spacing for air circulation
